title: Keyboard Manager doesn't work properly through remote desktop
author: endlessMagic

judgment.rationale: Multiple users describe Keyboard Manager remaps being applied inconsistently across Remote Desktop, including duplicate physical and mapped keys, broken Ctrl shortcuts, and toggle-state drift. The behavior and workaround request are concrete enough for a focused design investigation.
evidence: The original ESC/Caps Lock swap produces both ESC and Caps Lock remotely.
Additional users report Caps Lock/Ctrl and Right Alt remaps working locally but not reliably through RDP.
A closed duplicate describes the same pre-RDP versus post-RDP remapping mismatch.
The newest request proposes excluding Remote Desktop from local remapping.
judgment.recommended_action: Queue a focused design investigation of Keyboard Manager's RDP input boundary and application-exclusion semantics.

fix_assessment.rationale: The issue is reproducible and longstanding, but lightweight re-triage did not inspect the current input-hook implementation deeply enough to select between RDP-aware translation and app exclusion.

proposed_fixes.title: Define an RDP-safe Keyboard Manager remapping boundary
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Keyboard Manager's local low-level remap and Remote Desktop's keyboard capture both process stateful keys, allowing the physical key state and mapped key event to reach the remote session inconsistently.
plan: Trace key-down, key-up, toggle-state, and suppression behavior when mstsc.exe owns foreground input.
Choose between an RDP-aware event-handling correction and an explicit per-application bypass based on the trace.
Cover ESC/Caps Lock, Ctrl/Caps Lock, toggle keys, and Ctrl-based shortcuts in focused regression tests.
verification: Connect through Windows Remote Desktop and repeat each public remap without duplicate physical-key behavior.
Confirm local remaps and remote toggle-key state remain balanced after disconnecting.

confidence.rationale: The RDP boundary is consistently implicated, but public evidence does not establish whether suppression, toggle state, or RDP translation is the first failing layer.

issue_context.summary: Keyboard Manager remaps can leak both original and mapped key behavior into Remote Desktop sessions.
known_information: Local behavior is correct for some reporters while RDP behavior is not.
Disabling local Keyboard Manager can allow the remote machine's mapping to work.
inferences: The mapping boundary relative to RDP input capture is central.
An exclusion list may be a mitigation rather than a complete fix.
issue_context.analysis: The issue has sufficient cross-user reproduction for design work, but the correct input ownership model requires code-level investigation.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the current public issue body, labels, assignees, and up to the latest 20 public comments returned by GitHub.
Kept the existing dashboard read-only; no dashboard files were modified or published.

information_gaps.information: Whether the preferred product behavior is RDP-aware remapping or an explicit per-application bypass.
information_gaps.why_needed: This determines the supported interaction model.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Confirm the intended policy before implementation.

actions.label: Approve define an rdp-safe keyboard manager remapping boundary
actions.note: Approve/start the fork-side design workflow from this public-evidence fix plan. No upstream write occurs from this action.

actions.label: Reproduce Keyboard Manager doesn't work properly through remote desktop
actions.note: Maintainer-side reproduction reduces the recorded implementation uncertainty without asking the reporter to perform code investigation.

prerequisites: Two Windows systems or a reachable Windows Remote Desktop host.
steps: Swap Escape and Caps Lock locally.
Press the physical Caps Lock key in the remote session.
Repeat with Caps Lock/Ctrl and a Ctrl-based shortcut.
reproduce.expected_result: Only the mapped key behavior reaches the remote session.
reproduce.observed_result: The remote session can receive both original and mapped behavior or lose modifier shortcuts.
